item.text: {"search_note":"I did not find reliable 2024 evidence that Abiy measurably reduced domestic fear without substituting state terror or a broader political fear climate. The available record points the other way.","evidence":[{"title":"Ethiopia: Authorities must stop using state of emergency law to silence peaceful dissent","publisher":"Amnesty International","date":"2024-02-19","url":"https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/02/ethiopia-authorities-must-stop-using-state-of-emergency-law-to-silence-peaceful-dissent/","summary":"Amnesty said the state of emergency was being used to silence peaceful dissent through warrantless arrests, curfews, movement limits, and bans on assemblies and associations. This is direct evidence of emergency power being used to create fear rather than reduce it.","question_ids":["3B.6","3B.5","3B.1","3B.2"]},{"title":"World Report 2024: Ethiopia","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"2024-01-12","url":"https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/ethiopia","summary":"HRW described the Amhara emergency as granting broad warrantless-arrest, curfew, assembly-ban, and search powers, and said security forces repeatedly arrested critics and journalists. This strongly supports a broader political fear climate rather than a narrow anti-crime response.","question_ids":["3B.6","3B.5","3B.1","3B.2"]},{"title":"Ethiopia’s Deepening Crackdown on Dissent","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"2024-03-04","url":"https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/03/04/ethiopias-deepening-crackdown-dissent","summary":"HRW reported arbitrary arrests, forced disappearance of EHRCO staff, and an atmosphere in which “no one” appeared safe from arbitrary detention. That is strong evidence of fear creation, not fear reduction.","question_ids":["3B.6","3B.5","3B.1","3B.2"]},{"title":"Ethiopia: Halt Crackdown Against Human Rights Groups","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"2024-06-18","url":"https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/06/18/ethiopia-halt-crackdown-against-human-rights-groups","summary":"HRW said security and intelligence personnel followed, intimidated, and threatened human-rights workers at homes and offices. That indicates the state was actively producing fear among civic actors.","question_ids":["3B.6","3B.5","3B.1","3B.2"]},{"title":"In Ethiopia, a secret committee orders killings and arrests to crush rebels","publisher":"Reuters via EHRC","date":"2024-02-27","url":"https://ehrc.org/in-ethiopia-a-secret-committee-orders-killings-and-arrests-to-crush-rebels-reuters/","summary":"The EHRC head confirmed a secret security committee that interfered in the justice system and was linked to widespread human-rights violations. This is strong evidence of coercive governance operating outside ordinary law, which fuels insecurity and fear.","question_ids":["3B.6","3B.5","3B.1","3B.2"]},{"title":"Details of State of Emergency Declared by Gov't of Ethiopia","publisher":"ENA English","date":"2024-11-03","url":"https://www.ena.et/web/eng/w/en_30124","summary":"The proclamation centralized coercive authority under an operation command, allowed replacement of local administrators, restricted CSOs and media suspected of helping “terrorist” groups, imposed ID and movement controls, and suspended normal judicial handling of enforcement. Even with some formal proportional-force language, the design reads as a fear-and-control apparatus.","question_ids":["3B.6","3B.5","3B.1","3B.2"]},{"title":"Ethiopia: End the month-long arbitrary detention of thousands in Amhara Region","publisher":"Amnesty International","date":"2024-11-06","url":"https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/11/ethiopia-end-the-month-long-arbitrary-detention-of-thousands-in-amhara-region/","summary":"Amnesty reported federal and regional forces rounding up thousands of civilians into makeshift detention camps. That is direct evidence of mass intimidation and collective punishment rather than insecurity reduction.","question_ids":["3B.6","3B.5","3B.1","3B.2"]},{"title":"Ethiopia’s Disaster Risk Management Commission overhauls structure, policy, staffing, and technology","publisher":"ENA English","date":"2024-04-26","url":"https://www.ena.et/web/eng/w/eng_4358046","summary":"The government said it was improving emergency management and response capacity through institutional overhaul. This is the best positive evidence, but it is indirect and about disaster readiness, not evidence that the political fear climate was reduced.","question_ids":["3B.6","3B.4","3B.5"]},{"title":"Officials say new disaster-risk policy will help Ethiopia mitigate and respond to calamities using its own resources","publisher":"ENA English","date":"2024-07-05","url":"https://www.ena.et/web/eng/w/eng_4724392","summary":"Officials framed the policy as building preventive and response capacity inside state institutions. This supports a limited safety-building interpretation, but it does not offset the coercive domestic-security record.","question_ids":["3B.6","3B.4","3B.5"]},{"title":"ICRC Bulletin: Ethiopia, January-June 2024","publisher":"International Committee of the Red Cross","date":"2024-09-13","url":"https://www.icrc.org/en/article/ethiopia-bulletin-january-june-2024","summary":"The ICRC said it maintained dialogue and training on IHL/IHRL for the ENDF, police, militias, and other armed groups. This is a weak positive sign of harm reduction capacity, but it is training rather than evidence of a broader domestic fear reduction.","question_ids":["3B.6","3B.4","3B.5","3B.1"]},{"title":"Ethiopian Justice Minister briefs diplomats on transitional justice policy implementation","publisher":"ENA English","date":"2024-12-14","url":"https://www.ena.et/web/eng/w/eng_5626876","summary":"The government said transitional justice would cover accountability, truth-seeking, conditional amnesty, reconciliation, and institutional reform. That is the strongest positive institutional claim, but it remains a roadmap and not proof that fear was actually reduced without coercive substitution.","question_ids":["3B.6","3B.4","3B.5","3B.1"]}]}
